latest_final: The trick is the word "courses": here they are food courses (dishes in a meal), not academic classes. I was in a university dining hall or canteen where plates and trays are cleared promptly, but the "courses" were my meal's dishes, not my enrolled classes. I was eating there that evening. One of the dishes was not to my satisfaction, so I made a complaint or returned a dish in person to the staff about the food itself (not a complaint about seating, service, or a spill). The staff took this as a signal that I no longer wanted the meal, so they cleared the table, and all of my remaining uneaten dishes were taken away. Everyone—me, the staff—had left them uneaten, and it was not the case that I had finished or intended to leave; rather, my in-person food complaint caused the staff to clear all my "courses." I was not removed from my classes online, no system error or deadline was involved, and nobody used my account. The setup sentence about being an HKU student who must choose courses before a deadline misleads you into reading "courses" as academic classes, when in fact the evening's "courses" were the dishes of a meal that were cleared away after my complaint. (The exact nature of the complaint—e.g. that the dish was badly prepared—was not confirmed, so I do not rely on it.)
